newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Nov/Dec coffee sales seen 1.5 mln bags each.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Nov/Dec coffee sales seen 1.5 mln bags each.

text.p: Brazilian coffee exports should total around 1.5 million bags a month during November and December, said the head of the primary commodities department of the Industry and Commerce Ministry.
"In November we expect to see shipments of 1.5 million bags of which 1.2 million have already been loaded by November 24," said Mauricio Assis after a regular meeting with exporters.
"Registrations for December are also around 1.5 million bags and there are 515,000 bags already registered for export in January 1997," he added.
Assis added that with these numbers, Brazil expected to ship around nine million bags in the July to December period, in line with the quota agreed with other producing countries.
Exporters have already begun to express concern over supply in the following six months (January to June) when Brazil has been alloted a further six million bag exports.

"To ship six million bags will have to involve strict co-ordination between the coffee community and the government," said Oswaldo Aranha, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Federation (Febec).
An added factor is the growing expectation of a smaller coffee harvest in 1997/98, he added.
The government is currently working towards setting up the structure for an official coffee estimate which should be in place next year but "the feeling is that the crop will be small," Assis said.
One other option is to increase the size of sales of government stocks which currently have a monthly limit of 200,000 bags but which so far have been for much smaller quantities.
Assis said that the size of auctions would only be decided nearer to the time of each sale but already some exporters feel that even 200,000 bags a month would not be enough, Aranha said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
